_what: Corpus-overlap report for XQ_2020, per the run brief's trap 2. REPORT ONLY -- nothing here was acted on; this is a merge-level fact.

headline.verdict: ZERO overlap on all three keys. All eleven R-O16CBA lipidoids are new to the corpus. That is expected rather than lucky: the cyclic-benzylidene-acetal tail appears in no other curated paper, and a corpus-wide search for IL_names containing 'O16' or 'CBA' returns only the twelve 'Xue_siloxane_Si_n_O16' lipids, which are siloxanes.

THE_REAL_OVERLAP_IS_AT_THE_HEAD_GROUP._what: The eleven amine heads are the Xu-lab / Tufts catalogue numbering, and four of them are already in the corpus as the heads of a DIFFERENT library. This is invisible to a full-InChIKey comparison and is the kind of cross-source chemistry Result 3 cares about.

QL_2026.our_structures_agree_with_theirs: 4/4, byte-identical canonical SMILES; their source is a vendor catalogue name in the SI materials list, ours is the structure drawn in Figure 1C. This is check P11.

THE_REAL_OVERLAP_IS_AT_THE_HEAD_GROUP.shared_head_but_NOT_a_shared_lipid: No full structure is shared, so none of these would enter Stage 5's shared-lipid concordance. The commonality is the head group only.

THE_NAME_TOKEN_TRAP._what: 163 corpus IL_names begin with one of our eleven amine numbers, and they do NOT all mean the same thing. QL_2026's '113-L1-C6' uses 113 as the Xu amine number and its structure does contain our amine 113. BL_2024's '113-9', '113-22' and '113-23' use 113 as a series index in an unrelated naming scheme and contain no such head. Keying on the leading token across experiments would merge them.
THE_NAME_TOKEN_TRAP.the_rule: CLAUDE.md section 3: never key on IL_name alone across experiments - use the SMILES.
